## The failing lines (fix round `build/M0-c-03-fix-s2`, tests only unless the pins expose a defect)

**B-1 — the Q24 line's last clause: an unserved part is not pinned in S4's `report.unserved`.** The Q24 line requires
"an unserved gate that the rule leaves unserved is reported in the run (a counted outcome, never silent)", and the
brief names the kill-test "the unserved outcome not reported". Mutant **Z06** deletes the outward part's listing in
`routesFromSlice` (`stage.ts:278`, `} else unserved.push(\`${gate.id}/out\`);` becomes `}`). It **survives** NEAR
(84/84) and the related tests that run S4 through the chain (`ladders/rungs-route.test.ts`, `ladders/chain.test.ts`,
`pipeline/base/run.test.ts`, `edge/control.test.ts`: 36/36 at `PLAT_FUZZ_RUNS=1000`). A census inside
`plat/packages/*/{src,test}` and `plat/bench` finds no other reader of S4's `report.unserved`. The only tests that read
it are `frame.test.ts` and `water.test.ts`, and both assert `[]`. So Z06 survives the whole of (3). It changes an
honest input: on the plain small-river chain, seed 3207739920 (`i` = 142), `gate:1/out` is left unserved by the rule.
Its rungs are `another_site` from `bridge:1`, held false, 'no usable site in the band'; then `extra_bridge`
`notBuilt(M1)`; then `unserved` 'no path'. Its `report.unserved` is `['gate:1/out']`, and under Z06 it is `[]`. Since
the run's report does not carry S4's unserved parts either (note 17), S4's `report.unserved` is the one place that
lists the part. The round made seed 3535584350, its only earlier honest case, served, so nothing at stage level now pins
the listing.
*Required change:* pin a part the rule leaves unserved at stage level, for example seed 3207739920 in `frame.test.ts`:
`report.rungs` for `gate:1/out` equal to the three rungs above, `report.unserved` equal to `['gate:1/out']`, no
`gate:1/out` route, and ways = 2N − 1. Show Z06 red on it, and Z02 too (the 'no usable site' / 'no path' labels).

**B-2 — `deckOf` marks only wet edges, which no test pins.** `RouteGraph.deckOf` is documented as "the index of the
deck … a passable edge across water runs along, else −1". Mutant **Z20** drops the `wet(lattice, p, q)` test in
`routeGraph` (`route.ts:79`), so a dry edge within one spacing of a deck and within 30° of it is also given the deck.
It **survives** NEAR (84/84) and the whole RELATED@1000 run (207 files; 4 red: `hausdorff`, `span`,
`districts/integration` and `ladder-coverage/entry`). All four are red without the mutant too: the first two in the
tree's own gate run, and the last two in this seat's unmutated `after` mirror (they read files outside the mirror, or
the mirror's copy of in-flight foreign work). It changes an honest input: seed 3418200249 (`i` = 821), where
`gate:0/out` spans `bridge:1` with 11 points, and under Z20 it has 10. The approach node next to the deck end is folded
into the crossing's run. The output under Z20 passes S4's own checks, so it fails safely. But it is a different
committed course, it comes from an unpinned contract of the interface the N-54 (2) pin is about, and the item's earlier
rounds treated such survivors as blockers (B-6 and B-7, `checks/M0-c-03.md`). So the seat classes Z20 as a blocker. This
is a vetoable call: under N-45 it could instead be a hardening note.
*Required change:* a `routeGraph` pin that only wet edges carry a deck. On a synthetic river with one deck, every edge
with `deckOf` ≠ −1 meets a water face, and a dry edge along the deck within one spacing of an end answers −1 (or seed
3418200249's `gate:0/out` point count). Show Z20 red on it.

## Line 1 — N-54 (2): the `deckOf` −1 pin (CONFIRMED)

The new block "a deck with an end beyond the frame is no deck of S4's route graph (N-54 (2), C-0289; Q24)" in
`route.test.ts` builds a 40 m river across the whole frame and a deck that slants across it near the frame's north edge.
One end is 1 m beyond the frame, and the other is 11 m inside.
* Beyond, the pin asserts that `rg.decks` is `[]`, that every `deckOf` is −1, that `solve` finds no path, and that the
  ladder reports `[{ rung: 'unserved', why: 'no path' }]`.
* In the control the same deck is 1 m inside. There `rg.decks` holds it, at least 2 edges carry `deckOf` 0, and the
  route's one crossing is that deck.

The negative control was planted in the `mut` mirror's copy of `siting/lattice.ts`, never the tree. Mutant Z19 is
`const costs = framedCosts(site.frameRing, given)` → `const costs = given`, which is the lattice before C-0289. On the
backbone folder it gave "Tests 3 failed | 81 passed (84)". The pin failed. Both `frame.test.ts` seeds also failed:
"bridge:0: expected false to be true", the precondition that every deck in the lattice lies inside the frame. The
control passed. After the run the mirror's `lattice.ts` `cmp`-equals the tree's.

## Line 2 — Q24: the band retry on an empty band (CONFIRMED except where marked)

**The change read whole.** It is `routeLadder` in `route.ts:291–366`. The pre-round code gave up a deck. When no other
non-excluded deck had its midpoint within `searchBandCm` of the first deck given up, the code returned `unserved`
('approach') at once. Otherwise it re-solved with only the given-up decks excluded, and that re-solve could take a site
anywhere. Now, at the first give-up, every deck beyond that band is excluded, except a crossing the current course
already makes with a usable approach. The code records whether the band held another site (`bandEmpty`) and always
re-solves. With no course, it reports `another_site` held false ('no other site in the band' or 'no usable site in the
band'), then `extra_bridge` `notBuilt(M1)`. It then takes the slope rung when grade limits are given, and otherwise
`unserved` ('approach' or 'no path').

**The judgement (the seat's own, vetoable): I agree with C-0297.**
* §5.2's F-ROUTE row is triggered by `E_NO_PATH` or "an approach cannot meet a pinned bridge deck". Its first rung is
  "another crossing site on the reach within its search band". The rung serves a route that needs a crossing.
* With the given-up deck impassable, the re-solve is the same search §4.3 runs for any route. A course that reaches the
  frame dry needs no crossing, so leaving it `unserved` would break §4.3 *Result* ("through-roads continue to the
  context margin") and the item's roads-leaving = N, for want of a deck the road never needed.
* The pre-round result on seed 3535584350 came only from an unreachable beyond-frame deck counted in the band. So the
  frame cutting the band is not the lawful reason to leave a gate unserved. When no course exists, `unserved` is the
  lawful outcome and is reported.
* Two further points support the round. The band restriction is what §5.2's "within its search band" says, and it
  closes this file's earlier note 3. And the pre-round early return skipped the slope rung, against the ladder's order;
  now the slope rung runs when grade limits are given.
